title: Vanishing first cohomology separates disjoint closed subsets by global functions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: its point space is quasi-compact and its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Give $|X|$ the atlas topology on field-valued point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Use quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and cohomology of their underlying additive sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Suppose $H^1(X,F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent module $F$. For any disjoint closed subsets $Z_0,Z_1\subseteq|X|$, there is $a\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ such that $$Z_0\subseteq V(a),\qquad Z_1\subseteq V(a-1).$$ Here $V(b)$ is the set of points where evaluation of $b$ under a field-valued representative is zero; this is independent of the representative. Either or both closed subsets may be empty.

proof.text: If $Z_0$ is empty, take $a=1$; if $Z_1$ is empty, take $a=0$. These choices give the required inclusions directly, including when both subsets or $X$ are empty. In the remaining steps assume both closed subsets are nonempty.

By [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], give each $Z_j$ its reduced closed subspace structure, writing $i_j:Z_j\hookrightarrow X$ for the inclusion. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules], $Q_j=i_{j,*}\mathcal O_{Z_j}$ is quasi-coherent and the canonical map $q_j:\mathcal O_X\to Q_j$ is surjective. Also $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent directly from [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]: its local presentation is $0\to\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_X\to0$ (zero relations and one generator).

Form $r=(q_0,q_1):\mathcal O_X\to Q_0\oplus Q_1$. A finite direct sum here is the sectionwise product: $r(s)=(q_0(s),q_1(s))$ defines its two components. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-pushforward-geometric-stalks], $(Q_j)_{\bar x}=0$ when the geometric point $\bar x$ does not factor through $Z_j$. Since $Z_0\cap Z_1=\varnothing$, no geometric point factors through both. If it factors through one, the other stalk is zero and $r_{\bar x}$ is its surjective component $q_{j,\bar x}$; otherwise both target stalks are zero. The component is surjective because [lem-sfb-space-etale-conservative-geometric-points] preserves small colimits (hence epimorphisms) on stalks and $q_j$ is a sheaf epimorphism. This node also preserves finite products and detects epimorphisms, so $r$ is surjective.

Put $N=Q_0\oplus Q_1$ and $K=\ker r$. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], $N$ and $K$ are quasi-coherent. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], kernels are computed sectionwise, so the underlying abelian sheaf of $K$ is the kernel of the underlying map $r$. Surjectivity was proved on underlying stalks in the preceding step. Thus $0\to K\to\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{r}N\to0$ is short exact also as abelian sheaves, and the hypothesis of the item applies to give $H^1(X,K)=0$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to this short exact sequence in abelian sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, with $v=\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},-)$. The abelian category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Global sections mean compatible families of sections over all etale scheme charts, equivalently maps from the terminal sheaf; addition and kernels of these families are componentwise, so $v$ is additive and left exact. The canonical natural identification $R^0v=v$ is [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero]. Hence the relevant exact segment is $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\xrightarrow{\Gamma(r)}\Gamma(X,N)\to H^1(X,K)=0$, where cohomology is computed on underlying additive sheaves as required. Exactness says that every section of $N$ has a lift in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$.

The zero section of $\mathcal O_{Z_0}$ and unit section of $\mathcal O_{Z_1}$ give global sections of $Q_0$ and $Q_1$: in the chart-limit definition of direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], assign respectively $0$ and $1$ on every chart, compatibly with restriction. Pairing these gives $t=(0,1)\in\Gamma(X,N)$. Choose a lift $a\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ by the preceding step. Thus the two canonical restrictions of $a$ are $0$ and $1$.

To check the stated field-valued zero loci, let $x:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ represent a point in $Z_j$. By the base-change support assertion of [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], $Z_j\times_X\operatorname{Spec}L$ is a nonempty closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}L$. A closed subscheme of the spectrum of a field is either empty or the whole spectrum: its defining ideal is either the unit ideal or zero, by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $x$ factors through $Z_j$, and evaluation of the restrictions just obtained gives $a(x)=0$ for $j=0$ and $a(x)=1$ for $j=1$. Therefore $Z_0\subseteq V(a)$ and $Z_1\subseteq V(a-1)$. Evaluation commutes with extensions of the representative field, and a field extension is injective, so being zero is independent of the field-valued representative.

tool_uses.why: The canonical chart-limit definition of direct image supplies the compatible zero and unit sections; this is a general small-etale module tool, not a step of the trace-formula route.
The general sectionwise description of module kernels identifies the underlying abelian kernel; the unit gives no replacement for this ringed-site definition.
Its local free-presentation predicate verifies that the structure module is quasi-coherent; this is a foundational definition for algebraic spaces.
The general homological-algebra long exact sequence turns H1(K)=0 into surjectivity of global sections; the unit supplies no different cohomology sequence.
Enough injectives in abelian sheaves verifies the hypothesis of the general derived-functor theorem on the small etale site; this is a generic site tool.
The defining scheme-test quotient description shows a nonempty closed subscheme of Spec of a field is the whole spectrum; this is a generic definition, not a substitute route.

lean.statement: theorem exists_global_function_separating_closed {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X) (hH : ∀ (F : X.Modules) (_ : F.IsQuasicoherent), Subsingleton (@Sheaf.H _ _ _ ((sheafCompose X.etaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}).obj ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf X.structureSheaf).obj F)) inferInstance (HasExt.standard _) 1)) (Z₀ Z₁ : Set (Point X.obj.obj)) (hZ₀ : IsClosed Z₀) (hZ₁ : IsClosed Z₁) (hdisj : Disjoint Z₀ Z₁) : ∃ a : RingCat.sectionsSubring X.structurePresheaf, (∀ (T : X.EtaleSite) (x : X.etaleForget.obj T), schemePointMap T.obj.hom x ∈ Z₀ → (X.etaleForget.obj T).Γevaluation x (a.val (op T)) = 0) ∧ (∀ (T : X.EtaleSite) (x : X.etaleForget.obj T), schemePointMap T.obj.hom x ∈ Z₁ → (X.etaleForget.obj T).Γevaluation x ((a - 1).val (op T)) = 0)
lean.note: Global functions use RingCat.sectionsSubring of the recorded structurePresheaf. Both zero-locus inclusions are expressed equivalently on every etale chart by Scheme.Γevaluation at its points. The cohomology is Sheaf.H of the canonical ULift of the underlying additive sheaf, with HasExt.standard, avoiding infrastructure assumptions or any restriction on S. Absolute quasi-separatedness uses the existing def-sfb-space-absolute-quasi-separated interface, added to stmt_deps.
